title: Hands Fold a Paper Sheet
tests: Tests coherent hand anatomy, hand-object contact and a completed paper-folding action in one text-generated shot.

faults.what: The surface is plain white with no visible wood texture, rather than the requested wooden table.
The audio report indicates music or ambience with a peak of 0 dB, contrary to the explicit no-sound requirement.

judge.summary: The realistic overhead clip shows a convincing blue-paper fold and crease pressing, but uses a white surface instead of a wooden table and is not silent.

must_haves.item: Both human hands and the entire blue sheet remain visible on a wooden table.
must_haves.why: Both hands and the sheet remain within the sampled framing, with natural hand occlusion, but the surface appears plain white rather than wooden.

must_haves.item: The hands visibly bring one half of the sheet over the other, producing a folded sheet rather than an abrupt object replacement.
must_haves.why: The frames show a flat sheet, a lifted half held by both hands, and then a flattened folded sheet.

must_haves.item: The hands press along the resulting crease after folding.
must_haves.why: The later frames show fingers pressing the folded paper and smoothing the crease.

must_haves.item: Hands remain anatomically plausible, without extra or fused fingers, and make convincing contact with the paper.
must_haves.why: The visible hands have plausible anatomy and convincingly grip and press the paper, with no evident extra or fused fingers.

must_haves.item: The blue paper remains a single consistent object throughout the action.
must_haves.why: The sampled stages show one consistently blue sheet progressing naturally into a folded rectangle.

must_haves.item: The eight-second widescreen video uses one fixed overhead shot and has no sound.
must_haves.why: The supplied duration is eight seconds and the frames show consistent widescreen overhead framing, but the audio report indicates audible music or ambience rather than silence.
